content: 1. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of darunavir and cobicistat by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to potential interactions. 2. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Cobicistat and clarithromycin mutually increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir increases the levels or effects of cobicistat similarly. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Colchicine use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If coadministration is necessary, reduce colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing information. 7. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of copanlisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of crizotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may lead to QT prolongation. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the crizotinib dose to 250 mg once daily. 10. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of dabrafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of daridorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Long-term use of corticosteroids metabolized by CYP3A4 may lead to systemic corticosteroid effects, including Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine intranasal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dofetilide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin and liposomal doxorubicin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustments may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. 18. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of darunavir and cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration may result in loss of therapeutic effect and development of resistance. 19. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. 22. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of entrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 23. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of enzalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of darunavir. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. 25. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ergoloid mesylates by decreasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 26. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the levels or effects of erythromycin base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is coadministered with atazanavir or darunavir. 27. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for loss of virologic response. 28. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of eszopiclone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat and darunavir. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. 33. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of felbamate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fentanyl transdermal and transmucosal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl dose as needed. 35. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
